insight.title: Traffic Lights Wear Hoods to Stop You From Cheating
insight.subtitle: The metal visors over traffic lights aren't there to block the rain—they are designed to keep you from predicting the future.
insight.notificationHook: Why traffic lights wear those metal hoods

sections.text: Those long metal hoods over traffic lights look like umbrellas to shield the bulbs from rain or snow. But they actually have a much sneakier psychological job to do.
They act as visual blinders. By blocking the light from the sides, they prevent you from seeing when the cross-street’s light turns yellow, stopping you from floor-it anticipation.
If drivers could see neighboring lights changing, they would instinctively cheat and roll forward. The hoods force you to focus exclusively on your own lane, keeping intersections orderly and safe.
The hoods aren't blocking the weather—they’re blocking your impatience.
